examples.en: In autumn I picked apples at an orchard.
My grandfather runs a small orchard.
Pear trees stand in rows in the orchard.

examples.ko: 과수원 주인이 갓 딴 복숭아를 주셨어요.
examples.en: The orchard owner gave me peaches just picked.
In spring the orchard is full of white flowers.
We went on a field trip to an orchard.

explain: 채소를 키우는 곳은 '밭', 쌀을 키우는 곳은 '논', 과일나무를 키우는 곳은 과수원이에요. 일하는 사람은 '과수원을 하다', 과일을 따는 일은 '따다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 할머니 댁 옆에 사과 과수원이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is an apple orchard next to my grandmother's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 과일을 키우는지 앞에 넣어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the fruit name before it to say what is grown.

phrases.en: The orchard owner shared apples with us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과수원을 가진 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the person who owns the orchard.

phrases.en: On weekends I go to the orchard with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일을 따러 가는 곳으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a place you go to pick fruit.

explain_en: A place for vegetables is a '밭', for rice a '논', and for fruit trees a 과수원. The owner says '과수원을 하다' (run an orchard), and picking fruit uses '따다'.

examples.ko: 서울에서 동북쪽으로 한 시간쯤 가면 공원이 나와요.
examples.en: If you go northeast from Seoul for about an hour, you reach a park.
The typhoon is slowly moving toward the northeast.
Our school is northeast of City Hall.
Morning sunlight comes in through the northeast window.
According to the compass, that mountain is to the northeast.
The sky in the northeast is full of clouds.

explain: 일상에서는 '동북쪽'과 '북동쪽'을 둘 다 써요. 가는 방향은 '동북쪽으로', 있는 위치는 '동북쪽에'로 말해요. 반대 방향은 '서남쪽'이에요.

phrases.en: My house is northeast of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동북쪽'과 같은 뜻으로 둘 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 동북쪽, and both are used.

phrases.en: The bus goes toward the northeast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 방향을 말할 때 '으로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 으로 when talking about the direction of travel.

phrases.en: That park is in the northeast of downtown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 있는 위치를 말할 때 '에'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에 when saying where something is.

explain_en: In daily life both '동북쪽' and '북동쪽' are used. Use '동북쪽으로' for the direction you go and '동북쪽에' for where something is. The opposite direction is '서남쪽'.

examples.en: There are empty seats at the back of the bus.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 뒷부분이 앞부분보다 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: In this movie, the last part is more fun than the first part.
I have not read the last part of the book yet.

examples.ko: 저 건물 뒷부분에 작은 주차장이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small parking lot at the back of that building.
I fell yesterday, so the back of my head hurts.
I forgot the end of the story, so I looked it up again.

explain: 반대말은 '앞부분'이에요. 공간만 말할 때는 '뒤쪽'도 자주 써요. 뒷부분은 [뒤뿌분]으로 읽고, '뒤'와 '부분' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가요.

phrases.en: The first part of this book is a little boring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷부분'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 뒷부분.

phrases.en: I'll sit in the back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공간을 말할 때 '뒷부분' 대신 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common alternative to 뒷부분 when talking about space.

phrases.en: I haven't read the last part of the book yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이나 이야기의 끝쪽을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for the end of a book or story.

explain_en: The opposite is '앞부분' (front part). For plain space, '뒤쪽' (the back side) is also common. 뒷부분 is read [뒤뿌분], with a 사이시옷 (ㅅ) between '뒤' and '부분'.

examples.en: Please turn right at the next traffic circle.

examples.ko: 로터리를 한 바퀴 돌고 나서야 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I only found the road after going around the traffic circle once.

examples.ko: 아침마다 로터리 앞에서 차가 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: Every morning the traffic backs up a lot in front of the traffic circle.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 시청 앞 로터리 근처예요.
examples.en: My house is near the traffic circle in front of City Hall.
There is a big fountain in the middle of the traffic circle.
Is the meeting place the cafe across from the traffic circle?

explain: '시청 앞 로터리'처럼 장소 이름 뒤에 붙여 길 이름처럼 부르기도 해요. 도로 안내에서는 '회전교차로'라는 말도 써요. '로터리를 돌다'처럼 움직임을 나타내는 말과 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.example: 로터리를 돌아서 첫 번째 길로 가세요.
phrases.en: Go around the traffic circle and take the first road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌다'와 함께 운전 방향을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 돌다 it is used to give driving directions.

phrases.en: Please let me off in front of the traffic circle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택시나 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for taxis or meeting places.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the traffic circle

phrases.en: Let's meet at the traffic circle in front of City Hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소 이름과 함께 길 이름처럼 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a place name like a street name.

explain_en: People often attach it to a place name, as in '시청 앞 로터리', and use it like a road name. In road guidance the term '회전교차로' is also used. It often pairs with movement verbs, as in '로터리를 돌다'.

examples.ko: 국내선 탑승구가 어디예요? — 이 층 오른쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is the domestic flight gate? — It's on this floor, on the right.

examples.ko: 탑승구가 바뀌었으니 안내 방송을 잘 들으세요.
examples.en: The gate has changed, so listen carefully to the announcements.

examples.ko: 비행기 출발 삼십 분 전에 탑승구에 도착하세요.
examples.en: Please arrive at the boarding gate thirty minutes before departure.
I'm waiting for my family in front of the gate.

examples.ko: 저쪽 탑승구는 아직 문이 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: The gate over there is still closed.
It takes about ten minutes to walk to the gate.

explain: 공항에서 비행기에 타는 문이에요. 번호를 붙여 '십이 번 탑승구'처럼 말하고, 공항에서는 '게이트'라고 말하는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.en: Please go to boarding gate 12.
phrases.nuance_ko: 번호를 붙여서 위치를 말하는 가장 흔한 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to name a gate by number.

phrases.en: Where is the gate?
phrases.nuance_ko: 공항에서 '탑승구'를 말할 때 많이 쓰는 영어식 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The English-style word often used at airports instead of 'tapseunggu'.

phrases.en: I waited for my friend in front of the boarding gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만날 곳이나 기다릴 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a meeting or waiting spot.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the boarding gate

explain_en: It is the door at the airport where you board the plane. You attach a number, as in '십이 번 탑승구' (gate 12), and at airports people sometimes just say '게이트'.

examples.en: My Korean level is still beginner.
We take a level test and decide the class.
I'm happy because my level went up in the game.
This book is divided by level.
To raise your level you have to practice every day.
Try choosing a class that fits your level.

explain: 한국어 학원에서는 '급'이나 '단계'라는 말도 같이 써요. 게임이나 반 나누기에서 '레벨'이 자주 나와요. 실력 차이를 말할 때 '레벨이 다르다'고 하면 차이가 크다는 느낌이에요. 일반적인 수준 이야기에서는 '수준'도 써요.

phrases.en: That friend's game level is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임이나 실력의 단계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a game or skill level.

phrases.en: I finally leveled up in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단계가 올라갈 때 쓰는 말로 게임에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving up a level, common in games.

phrases.en: My Korean level has improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일반적으로 실력이나 정도를 말할 때는 '수준'이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For general skill or standard, 수준 sounds more natural.

explain_en: Korean language schools also use 급 and 단계 alongside it. 레벨 comes up often in games and when sorting classes. Saying 레벨이 다르다 about skill implies a big gap. For general standards, 수준 is also used.

examples.en: What made you so angry?
Why on earth did you go all the way there alone?
What's so important about that?

examples.ko: 이 일을 뭣부터 시작해야 할지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know what to start with first on this job.

examples.ko: 오늘은 뭣 하나 제대로 되는 게 없어요.
examples.en: Today, not a single thing is going right.

examples.ko: 이 많은 걸 뭣에 쓰려고 샀어요?
examples.en: What did you buy this much for?

explain: '무엇'을 줄인 '뭐'보다 조금 거칠거나 강조하는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 '뭣 때문에', '뭣 하러', '뭣도 모르고'처럼 굳은 짝으로 써요. 평소 말은 '뭐'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: without knowing anything
phrases.nuance_ko: 사정을 전혀 모른 채 행동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts without knowing the situation at all.

explain_en: It feels a little rougher or more emphatic than '뭐', the short form of '무엇'. It mostly appears in set pairs such as '뭣 때문에', '뭣 하러', and '뭣도 모르고'. In ordinary speech, '뭐' is more natural.

dis.h: clipped form used in set phrases
gh: full form; formal, written or spoken

p.n: Same meaning; the replacement is the plain spoken form.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 쓰는 것과 다르게 발음되는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: This word is often pronounced differently from how it's written.
The word for flower plus a subject marker is pronounced 'kkochi', so the final consonant links to the next syllable.
The name of the ancient kingdom Silla is pronounced 'Silla', so the sound differs from the spelling.
The ㅎ at the end of the syllable in the word for 'good' is not pronounced.

examples.ko: 외국인 이름은 한국어로 다르게 발음될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Foreign names can be pronounced differently in Korean.

examples.ko: 이 이름은 나라마다 다르게 발음되고 있어요.
examples.en: This name is pronounced differently in each country.

explain: '발음하다'는 사람이 소리 내는 것이고, '발음되다'는 글자나 단어가 어떤 소리로 나는지 말할 때 써요. '[꼬치]로 발음되다'처럼 소리를 대괄호로 함께 적기도 해요.

phrases.en: This letter is pronounced differently in each word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어에 '다르게'를 붙여 쓰기와 소리가 다를 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds 'differently' to say the sound doesn't match the spelling.

phrases.en: '밭이' is pronounced [바치].
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 소리를 대괄호로 적고 '~로 발음되다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Write the actual sound in brackets and add '~로 발음되다'.

phrases.en: In this word, 'ㅎ' is hardly pronounced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자는 있지만 소리가 나지 않을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for when a letter is written but not heard.

explain_en: '발음하다' is a person making the sound, while '발음되다' says what sound a letter or word comes out as. Learners often write the sound in square brackets, as in '[꼬치]로 발음되다'.

examples.ko: 고향 친구가 감을 한 상자 보내왔어요.
examples.en: A friend sent me a box of persimmons from their hometown.
Grandmother sends us kimchi every year.
The company sent the news that I passed by email.
Someone sent me a strange text message yesterday.

examples.ko: 외국에 있는 언니가 사진을 보내오면 가족이 다 모여서 봐요.
examples.en: When my older sister abroad sends photos, the whole family gathers to look.

examples.ko: 학교에서 안내문을 보내오면 꼭 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: If the school sends a notice, be sure to read it.

explain: '보내다'는 내가 보내는 것이고, '보내오다'는 상대가 나에게 보내서 도착하는 것이에요. 편지, 소식, 선물, 문자에 많이 써요. 내가 상대에게 보낼 때는 '보내다'나 '보내 주다'를 써요.

phrases.en: An old friend sent me a letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 나에게 편지를 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sends a letter to me.

phrases.en: My aunt sent me a birthday present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높일 사람이면 '보내오시다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For someone you respect, say 보내오시다.

phrases.en: My younger sibling sent me the photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보내오다'보다 더 일상적이고, 누가 누구에게 보낼 때든 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual than 보내오다, and usable whoever is sending to whom.

explain_en: '보내다' is when I send something, while '보내오다' is when the other person sends it and it reaches me. It is common with letters, news, gifts and text messages. When I send to someone, I use '보내다' or '보내 주다'.

en: counseling center; consultancy; counseling service agency

examples.en: If you have a worry, try going to a counseling center.

examples.ko: 이 상담소는 무료로 이야기를 들어 줘요.
examples.en: This counseling center listens to you for free.
The counseling center is on the third floor of the building.
My friend told me about a counseling center.
I talked with a counselor for an hour at the counseling center.
Some counseling centers also require a reservation.

explain: 고민이나 문제를 전문가와 이야기하러 가는 곳이에요. '법률 상담소', '청소년 상담소'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여 써요. 학교 안에서는 '상담실'이라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I got free help at a legal counseling center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 분야를 붙여서 어떤 상담인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A field name before it shows the type of counseling.

phrases.example: 청소년 상담소는 학생들의 고민을 들어 줘요.
phrases.en: The youth counseling center listens to students' worries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대상을 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The target group can also come first.

phrases.en: I talked with a teacher in the school counseling room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 안에 있는 작은 공간은 '상담실'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small room inside a school is 상담실.

explain_en: It is a place where you go to talk about worries or problems with a professional. The field comes first, as in '법률 상담소' (legal) or '청소년 상담소' (youth). Inside a school it may be called '상담실'.

en: to shake hands; to shake one's hand

examples.en: I shake hands with people I meet for the first time.
Yesterday I shook hands with the new boss.
I will shake hands with the guest first tomorrow.
The hand I shook was very warm.
The two smiled, shook hands, and parted.
I was really happy to shake hands with my teacher.

explain: 악수하는 상대 뒤에 '와/과'나 '하고'를 붙여서 '친구와 악수하다'처럼 써요. '악수를 하다'로 띄어 써도 같아요.

phrases.en: We shake hands with each other before the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악수하다'와 뜻이 같고, 띄어 쓰면 '를'이 들어가요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword, with the object particle added when spaced.

phrases.en: Since we've just met, shall we shake hands?
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 하자고 제안할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to propose doing it together.

phrases.en: When we meet, we shake hands and greet each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 두 동작을 이어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Joins two actions with '-go'.

explain_en: The other person takes '와/과' or '하고', as in '친구와 악수하다'. You can also split it as '악수를 하다' with the same meaning.

en: to be booked; to be reserved in advance

examples.en: The hotel room is already booked.

examples.ko: 이 자리는 다른 손님 이름으로 예약됐어요.
examples.en: This seat has been reserved under another guest's name.
Once it's booked, I'll let you know by text.
I went to the hospital at the booked time.
The ticket wasn't booked, so I applied again.
After the restaurant was booked, I told my friends.

explain: 자리나 시간이 이미 잡혀 있을 때 써요. '예약돼 있어요'가 가장 흔해요. 내가 하는 행동은 '예약하다'예요. 식당과 병원은 '예약', 친구와 만나는 일은 '약속'을 써요.

phrases.en: I can't make a reservation online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예약하려 해도 되지 않을 때 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in conversation when a booking can't be made.

phrases.en: Please sit in the reserved seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 잡아 둔 자리를 말할 때 명사 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun for a seat already reserved.

phrases.example: 식당에 가기 전에 예약됐는지 확인해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please check whether the reservation went through before going to the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예약이 제대로 되었는지 알아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking that a booking was properly made.

explain_en: It is used when a seat or time slot is already secured, and 예약돼 있어요 is the most common form. What you do yourself is 예약하다. Use 예약 for restaurants and clinics, and 약속 for meeting a friend.
